newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks end higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks end higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Colombian stocks ended higher on foreign fund buying in a market that saw the collapse of President Ernesto Samper's economic emergency plan as either neutral or favorable for equities, brokers said.

Medellin's IBOMED general price index closed up 0.17 percent at 16,689.92 on 1.1 billion pesos in trading volume. Bogota's IBB rose 0.76 percent, meanwhile, ending the day at 1,079.11 on 1.7 biliion pesos in trade.
"The Constitutional Court's decision was liked," one broker said. The court overturned Samper's emergency plan to plug a gaping fiscal deficit with new taxes imposed by decree.

Business leaders had criticized the emergency plan as inflationary since it included a six percent tax on all new foreign loans and promised to drive up the cost of imports, many of which are traditionally financed abroad.

The day's winners included brewer Bavaria SA, flagship of the Santo Domingo business group and Colombia's most actively traded stock since September of last year. It closed up 1.15 percent in Bogota at 6,980 pesos per share.
Other winners included Banco Ganadero, whose ordinary stock rose 1.77 percent to end at 344 pesos per share in Bogota.

Compania Suramericana de Seguros, the insurance giant belonging to the powerful Sindicato Antioqueno conglomerate, was also among gainers. It closed up 1.17 percent in the capital at 22,410 pesos per share.

The day's losers were led by Carulla, which fell 1.38 percent in Bogota after it was downgraded by Santander Investment from market perform to underperform because of disappointing 1996 earnings and an increasingly competitive food retailing environment. Carulla's stock, which got a buy rating from ING Barings nonetheless, ended at 3,550 pesos a share.
